names.note: saint.gr prints the name in Latin letters and in no Greek form at all, «Άγιος Dubritius», on 14 Νοεμβρίου; the form is recorded exactly as the page has it, as `lang: "en"` on the `cedd-the-bishop` precedent, because the page gives nothing to transliterate from.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Dubritius»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The whole notice is one sentence — «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ουαλού Αγίου» — we have no details of the Welsh saint's life. **No `types`**: the page gives him no rank, not even the «Όσιος» or «Ιερομάρτυς» its own lines usually carry, and the field is left out rather than guessed; the precedents in this wave are `iltud` and `justus-10-november`, two other western saints saint.gr keeps with no life. **No `dates`, no `locations`, no `related`, no hymn.** The entry carries no asterisk and not the «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence — the page's silence here is about the life, not about the saint, and that is the distinction §10 of the Greek brief turns on.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (2 October 2026).
